title: AI Coding Practice for Developers
excerpt: Real tickets in a real codebase, with an AI teammate that makes mistakes and a client who checks your work. Your first ticket is free.
content_html:
AI CODING PRACTICE

Practice coding
with AI on real tickets.

Five codebases in Python and JavaScript. Find out what the client needs, direct your AI teammate, and deliver. If something’s wrong, it comes back.

About 10 minutes. Marta is waiting.

HOW A TICKET GOES.

Ask. Direct.
Check. Deliver.

It’s how teams work with AI now. The hard part isn’t typing the code: it’s knowing what to build and catching what’s wrong.

  1. A client writesMarta: two families came for the same e-bike, and the system let both of them book it. That’s all she says at first.
  2. Ask what happenedShe only answers what you ask, and she won’t think of everything.
  3. Direct your AI teammateIt reads your chat with her, writes the code and runs the tests. It also makes the mistakes real AI makes.
  4. DeliverMarta tries it. She accepts it, or sends it back with what a customer ran into, and you find the case behind it. Each send-back costs points.

FIVE SEASONS.

Five codebases.
30 tickets.

Each season is one business and one codebase, with six tickets: a feature, a review of the AI’s code, a bug, a slow page, tests, and a change that has to reach every part of the code. Each ticket starts from a working version of the last.

  • Lakeside WheelsA bike rental: weekend prices, late fees, double bookings, 200,000 bookings.Season 0 · Python · First ticket free
  • Mossgate TeasA tea shop: a spring sale, refunds, a cent too much, a slow monthly report.Season 1 · Python
  • Larkspur PhysioA physio clinic: weekly sessions, reminder texts, the clocks going back.Season 2 · Python
  • Bramble Hill MuseumMuseum members: the ticket desk’s file, duplicates, members on the list twice.Season 3 · Python
  • Fernhill EatsFood delivery: fees by distance, the nearest courier, two couriers for one order.Season 4 · JavaScript

YOUR SKILLS.

Scored on how you work,
not just the result.

Every ticket ends with scores from what you did. Ask: did you find what the client needed? Direct: did the AI build it right? Verify: did you catch its mistakes? Protect: did what worked keep working? Performance: is it fast enough? Your tech lead adds one thing to do differently next time.

You don’t have to read the code: you try cases and check what comes out. The code is always there if you want it.

WHAT’S INCLUDED.

Your first ticket
is free.

Talking to the client is always free. Your AI teammate’s replies come with your plan, and credits add more: 1 credit is 2 replies.

FREE ACCOUNT

1ticket, Lakeside Wheels’ first, with 25 AI teammate replies

PRO

25tickets in five seasons, 50 AI teammate replies a month, every AlgoCademy lesson and mock interviews. The 7-day free trial opens every ticket, with 25 replies.

PACK

100credits for $19.99: 200 replies

PACK

300credits for $49.99: 600 replies

Packs never expire. They’re a one-time payment for anyone, and they’re used after the replies your plan includes.

See PRO plans

Do I need to read the code?

No. You find out what the client needs, tell your AI teammate, try cases and deliver. The code is there for anyone who wants it, and you can always write it yourself.

Which languages?

Python in Seasons 0 to 3, JavaScript (Node.js) in Season 4.

Is the AI teammate a real AI?

Yes. It writes code from what you tell it and runs the project’s tests. Each ticket also plants a few mistakes of the kind real AI tools make, so there’s always something to catch.

How is it different from interview practice?

In an interview you solve a problem alone. Here you work the way a team does now: with a client, an AI teammate and a codebase that grows from ticket to ticket.

New to coding?

Start with Booly’s Dev Agency: clients ask for apps and Booly, our AI, builds them. No code to write.

NO CARD NEEDED.

Your first ticket
is waiting.

Marta wants weekend prices. Find out what she really needs.

5 seasons · Python and JavaScript
